items.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So one time we had this duet concert in Italy. Just me and Scott.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. But you know with players like Harry Allen, you know, wonderful tenor player. We go on stage and until the very last minute Harry doesn’t know what he’s going to play. And then he’ll start something and we play it. That sometimes is risky but you know, I remember a few years ago with Scott Hamilton, another wonderful tenor player. I was exchanging this opinion of mine about the freedom of not having a set list. And I wanted to see what was his feeling about it. And he said, “thank goodness that at…

play something. Why do I have to make a set list before?” So one time we had this duet concert in Italy. Just me and Scott. And it was a beautiful church and we had no microphones. Just the piano and the saxophone. And with the perfect acoustics. Not too dry but not too wet. You know what I mean? And so I said, “Scott, let’s do this kind of concert. You start with any song you want. And if I know it I’ll join you. Otherwise you play by yourself. And then I’ll start with a song and of course you’ll know it,”…
Yeah. Then it becomes sort of like a competition.
